text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures surged by around a third of a point on Tuesday as U.S. inflation figures and a benign domestic economic picture spured professional demand. Gains, which pushed Bunds above the psychologically important 101.00 level, appeared to put the market back on an upward course after losses in recent weeks. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.12, up 0.25 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts closed higher on Tuesday after hitching a ride on the back of rising U.S. Treasuries, buoyed by evidence of benign inflationary pressures in the U.S. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-24/32, up 7/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures posted gains for the six consecutive session to settle at their highest level since February 2, 1994, after U.S. economic reports allayed fears of an interest rate rise and a favourable European economic backdrop continued to attract cash buyers. The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.04, up 0.38. from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures scaled a new record high of 130.83 on the December LIFFE contract after a slow start, spurred on by a subdued December U.S. inflation reading, but closed a touch short of the day's peak. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.70 up 0.37 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries popped higher, with the 30-year long bond gaining roughly half-a-point, after reassuringly benign consumer inflation numbers were released by the U.S. Labor Department. Treasuries appeared unperturbed by a healthy increase in December retail sales data, which were issued simultaneously. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-9/32, up 28/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.78 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tuesday's Tokyo session slightly higher in dealer-led trade. The March closed up 0.06 at 125.73. The volume was 42,823 contracts. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 125.59, down 0.18 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - The pace of new issues was at a more manageable level on Tuesday morning with business dominated by TEPCO's launch of a $1.0 billion bond.
Tokyo Electric Power's 10-year, reoffered 32 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, was the largest deal so far this year.
